Q1726: Capital of Bavaria on the Isar River, north of the Alps; Germany's third-largest city.
Hosts the Oktoberfest, the world's largest beer festival, every autumn.
Headquarters of BMW, Siemens and Allianz; home of FC Bayern Munich.
Hosted the 1972 Summer Olympics; Hitler's 1923 Beer Hall Putsch took place here.
Q495: Capital of Piedmont on the Po River, surrounded by the Alps.
Capital of the House of Savoy and the first capital of united Italy (1861–1865).
Home of Fiat and Juventus; the Shroud of Turin is kept in its cathedral.
The Egyptian Museum is one of the largest outside Egypt; hosted the 2006 Winter Olympics.
Q427488: City in northeastern Sichuan near Chongqing and Shaanxi.
Has large natural gas fields, including the Puguang field.
Known for its local lantern shadow puppetry and Ba culture.
Q43196: City in Ohio on the Ohio River, across from Kentucky.
Grew as a river port and pork-packing centre ('Porkopolis') in the 19th century.
Home of Procter & Gamble and the first professional baseball team (Red Stockings, 1869).
Known for Cincinnati chili, served on spaghetti.
Q71266: City in western Hubei on the Yangtze, at the eastern end of the Three Gorges.
The Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest power station, and the Gezhouba Dam are here.
Birthplace of the poet Qu Yuan, honoured by the Dragon Boat Festival.
Was a key battle site in the Three Kingdoms period (Battle of Yiling).
Q1335: Capital of Uruguay, on the Río de la Plata; home to about a third of Uruguayans.
Founded by the Spanish in the 1720s as a fortress against the Portuguese.
Hosted the first FIFA World Cup in 1930 at the Estadio Centenario.
Known for its long riverside promenade (Rambla) and mate drinking.
Q1055: Germany's second-largest city and a city-state, on the Elbe.
A leading city of the medieval Hanseatic League; its port is the third-largest in Europe.
The Speicherstadt warehouse district is a World Heritage Site; the Elbphilharmonie concert hall opened in 2017.
The Beatles played in its Reeperbahn clubs before they became famous.
Q456: France's third city, at the confluence of the Rhône and Saône.
Founded by the Romans as Lugdunum, capital of Roman Gaul.
A historical silk-weaving centre; the Lumière brothers invented cinema here.
Considered France's capital of gastronomy (bouchons); its old town is a World Heritage Site.
Q372791: City in southwestern Shandong on the Grand Canal.
Includes Qufu, birthplace of Confucius, with his temple, mansion and family cemetery (World Heritage Site).
Also home of Zoucheng, birthplace of Mencius.
A port on the Grand Canal and a big coal-mining area.
Q836527: City in western Tamil Nadu, the 'Knitwear Capital of India'.
Exports cotton knitwear and T-shirts to brands around the world.
Lies on the Noyyal River, which has suffered from dyeing pollution.
Q1781: Capital of Hungary, formed in 1873 from Buda and Óbuda on the hilly west bank and Pest on the flat east bank of the Danube.
The Danube banks, Buda Castle and the Parliament Building are a World Heritage Site.
Famous for thermal baths, like Széchenyi and Gellért, and the first metro on the European continent (1896).
Q37320: City in Ohio on the shore of Lake Erie.
Founded in 1796 by Moses Cleaveland; grew as a steel and oil city — Rockefeller founded Standard Oil here.
Home of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (the term 'rock and roll' was popularised by a Cleveland DJ).
The Cuyahoga River fire of 1969 helped start the US environmental movement.
Q57787: City in northern Jiangsu on the old course of the Yellow River and the Grand Canal.
Birthplace of Xiang Yu, the warlord who fought Liu Bang for the empire after the Qin.
Famous for baijiu liquors such as Yanghe and Shuanggou.
Hometown of JD.com founder Richard Liu.
Q170115: Summer capital of Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, on the Jhelum River in the Kashmir Valley.
Known for Dal Lake with its houseboats and shikara boats, and the Mughal gardens like Shalimar Bagh.
Famous for Kashmir shawls (pashmina), papier-mâché and saffron.
Located in the disputed Kashmir region claimed by both India and Pakistan.
Q200713: City in Maharashtra, officially renamed Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in 2023.
Named after Mughal emperor Aurangzeb; his tomb and the 'Bibi Ka Maqbara' (a smaller Taj Mahal) are here.
Gateway to the Ajanta and Ellora caves, both World Heritage Sites.
Known for Himroo and Paithani silk weaving.
Q6397066: Capital of Fars province in southwest Iran; called the city of poets, gardens and wine.
Burial place of the poets Hafez and Saadi, whose tombs are pilgrimage sites.
Capital of Iran under the Zand dynasty in the 18th century.
Persepolis, the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, is about 60 km away; the Pink Mosque is famous for its stained glass.
Q58560: Port city on the Bohai Sea in Hebei, about 300 km east of Beijing.
Named after Qin Shi Huang, the first emperor, who is said to have visited.
The Great Wall meets the sea at Shanhaiguan ('Old Dragon's Head') here.
Beidaihe, the summer resort of China's leaders, is part of the city.
Q41819: The largest city in Missouri, on the Missouri River at the Kansas border.
Has more fountains than almost any city except Rome — 'City of Fountains'.
Famous for Kansas City barbecue and its jazz history.
Its twin Kansas City lies across the state line in Kansas.
Q16567: Capital of Ohio and its largest city, where the Scioto and Olentangy rivers meet.
Named after Christopher Columbus; founded in 1812 as the planned state capital.
Home of Ohio State University, one of the largest universities in the US.
Often used as a test market for new products because it is so 'average'.
Q3859: Capital of Rwanda, on rolling hills in the centre of the country.
Founded in 1907 as a German outpost; became the capital at independence in 1962.
The Kigali Genocide Memorial remembers the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi.
Known as one of Africa's cleanest and safest cities; plastic bags are banned.
Q144663: Second-largest city of Hunan, on the Xiang River.
Mount Heng (Nanyue), one of China's Five Great Mountains, is nearby.
Site of the 1944 Defence of Hengyang, one of the longest battles of the war against Japan.
Legend says wild geese flying south stop at its Huiyan peak.
Q324293: City in northern Henan; site of Yin, the last capital of the Shang dynasty.
The oracle bones, the oldest Chinese writing (about 1200 BC), were found here.
The Yinxu ruins are a World Heritage Site; home of the National Museum of Chinese Writing.
The Red Flag Canal, cut through cliffs in the 1960s, is in the prefecture.
Q74957: Steel city in Liaoning, south of Shenyang; the name means 'saddle mountain'.
Home of Anshan Iron and Steel (Angang), one of China's biggest steelmakers.
Has a very large jade Buddha and the nearby Qianshan mountains.
Tanggangzi hot springs were a favourite of the last emperor Puyi.
Q59213: City in northern Guangdong on the Bei River; Guangdong's largest prefecture by area.
Known for rafting, hot springs and karst caves, a weekend escape from Guangzhou.
Q1754: Capital of Sweden, built on 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea.
Founded around 1252; its old town Gamla stan is one of the best-preserved medieval centres in Europe.
The Nobel Prizes (except Peace) are awarded here every December.
Home of the Vasa Museum with a 17th-century warship, and of Spotify; called the 'Venice of the North'.
Q4020440: Administrative centre of Tegal Regency in Central Java.
Known for a fragrant jasmine black tea and the local tea culture called moci (tea in clay pots with rock sugar).
Q83387: The largest Kurdish-majority city in Turkey, on the Tigris River.
Its massive black basalt city walls (about 6 km long) are among the longest in the world; with the Hevsel Gardens a World Heritage Site.
Inhabited for about 10,000 years; called Amida in antiquity.
Q201832: City in Uttar Pradesh, about 130 km southeast of Delhi.
Home of Aligarh Muslim University, founded in 1875 by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
Known as the 'lock city' for its lock-making industry.
Was called Koil in earlier times.
Q119219: Twin industrial city next to Pune in Maharashtra.
One of India's biggest car-making centres (Tata Motors, Bajaj, Mercedes-Benz).
Grew rapidly since the 1960s; also an IT hub around Hinjawadi.
Q189633: City in Guangxi on the Li River; the name means 'forest of osmanthus'.
Famous karst landscape: 'Guilin's scenery is the best under heaven' — the Li River view is on the 20-yuan note.
The Reed Flute Cave and Elephant Trunk Hill are well-known sights.
Q23430: Capital of Mongolia, on the Tuul River at about 1,300 m; the coldest capital city in the world.
Started in 1639 as a moving monastery camp (Urga) and settled at its present site in 1778.
Renamed Ulaanbaatar ('Red Hero') in 1924 under communist rule.
Home to about half of Mongolia's people; many live in ger (yurt) districts.
Q45208: Jilin City, in China's northeast, lies on the Songhua River and was the original capital of Jilin province.
Famous for 'rime ice' (wusong): trees along the river coated in white frost in winter.
Co-hosted the 2007 Asian Winter Games; known for the Beidahu ski resort.
Q4093: Scotland's largest city, on the River Clyde.
Was the 'second city of the British Empire' and a world centre of shipbuilding.
Home to the University of Glasgow (1451) and the Art Nouveau architect Charles Rennie Mackintosh.
Famous for the football rivalry between Celtic and Rangers.
Q1342: City in Pennsylvania where the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers form the Ohio.
Called 'the Steel City': Andrew Carnegie's steelworks made it the US steel capital.
Has 446 bridges, more than almost any city in the world.
Home of Carnegie Mellon University and the Andy Warhol Museum.
Q1478: City in Metro Manila, the fourth-most populous in the Philippines.
Birthplace of the Katipunan revolution: Andrés Bonifacio started the 1896 revolt against Spain here.
Split into two separate parts after Quezon City took much of its land in 1949.
Q223587: City in the Nile Delta, capital of Dakahlia Governorate, on the Damietta branch of the Nile.
The name means 'the victorious', after the Egyptian victory over the Seventh Crusade in 1250.
King Louis IX of France was captured and held here.
Known for its university and medical centres.
Q37100: New Zealand's largest city, on a narrow isthmus between two harbours.
Built on a field of about 50 volcanoes, like Mount Eden and Rangitoto Island.
Nicknamed the 'City of Sails' for its many boats; hosted the America's Cup.
Has the largest Polynesian population of any city in the world.
Q883: Russia's third-largest city and the largest in Siberia, on the Ob River.
Founded in 1893 where the Trans-Siberian Railway crossed the Ob.
Akademgorodok, a science town, is a major Russian research centre.
Has one of the largest opera and ballet theatres in Russia.
Q3826: Capital of Oman, on the Gulf of Oman with the Hajar Mountains behind it.
A trading port for centuries; held by the Portuguese in the 16th–17th centuries, whose forts Jalali and Mirani still stand.
Known for its low white buildings, the Muttrah corniche and souq, and the Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque.
Was capital of a maritime empire reaching Zanzibar.
Q571808: City in eastern Guangxi on the Xi River system; formerly Gui County.
An inland river port and a centre of sugar cane and the 'lotus city'.
Q1265617: Small town in Murshidabad district, West Bengal, on the Ganges near Bangladesh.
A centre of bidi (hand-rolled cigarette) making.
Proposed as a river-trade point with Rajshahi in Bangladesh.
Q231318: Capital of Johor state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, across the strait from Singapore.
Connected to Singapore by the Causeway, one of the world's busiest land crossings.
Founded in 1855 by Sultan Abu Bakar.
Home of Legoland Malaysia and the Iskandar development region.
Q80053: Capital of East Azerbaijan in northwest Iran; Iran's main Azerbaijani (Turkic) city.
Its historic bazaar is one of the largest covered bazaars in the world (World Heritage Site).
Was a capital of several Persian dynasties, incl. the Ilkhanate and early Safavids.
Q205922: The Zhalong wetland nearby is a famous breeding area of the red-crowned crane.
A heavy-industry centre known for railway cars and machine tools.
Home to Daur and Manchu minorities.
Q72945: City in southeastern Shanxi on the Shangdang plateau.
A strategic area in Chinese history, including the Battle of Changping (260 BC).
Important for coal and the Taihang Mountains scenery.
Q36312: The largest city in Alberta, where the Bow and Elbow rivers meet near the Rocky Mountains.
Centre of the Canadian oil and gas industry.
Hosts the Calgary Stampede, a huge rodeo and festival every July.
Hosted the 1988 Winter Olympics; gateway to Banff National Park.
Q83114: Municipality in Rio de Janeiro state, across Guanabara Bay from Rio.
The second most populous municipality in the state.
Mostly a working-class commuter city, next to Niterói.
Q92277: Jilin City, in China's northeast, lies on the Songhua River and was the original capital of Jilin province.
The only major Chinese city that shares its name with its province.
Famous for 'rime ice' (wusong): trees along the river coated in white frost in winter.
Q200019: Second city of Rajasthan, at the edge of the Thar Desert; founded in 1459 by Rao Jodha.
Called the 'Blue City' for the blue-painted houses below Mehrangarh Fort.
Capital of the Marwar kingdom; the Umaid Bhawan Palace is one of the largest private homes in the world.
Jodhpur riding trousers are named after it.
Q223920: The Republic of the Congo's second city and economic centre, its main port on the Atlantic.
Centre of the country's offshore oil industry.
End of the Congo–Ocean Railway to Brazzaville, built in the 1920s–30s at the cost of many lives.
Q41087: Capital of North Carolina, nicknamed the 'City of Oaks'.
Named after Sir Walter Raleigh, who sponsored the lost Roanoke Colony.
Part of the Research Triangle with Durham and Chapel Hill, a big centre of tech and research.
Home of North Carolina State University.
Q3238: Capital of Honduras, in a mountain valley; forms one capital district with Comayagüela.
Became the capital in 1880, replacing Comayagua.
Grew from a Spanish silver-mining town; the name may mean 'silver hills'.
Its airport, Toncontín, was notorious for its difficult landing (now replaced by Palmerola).
Q16665884: Metropolitan authority in southeastern France around Marseille and Aix-en-Provence, created in 2016.
Marseille, France's oldest city, was founded by Greeks as Massalia around 600 BC; its port is France's largest.
Aix-en-Provence is the city of the painter Cézanne.
Known for bouillabaisse, Marseille soap and the Calanques national park.
Q44210: Argentina's second city, in the centre of the country by the Sierras Chicas.
Founded in 1573; its Jesuit Block and the oldest Argentine university (1613) are a World Heritage Site.
Nicknamed 'La Docta' (the learned); the 1918 student reform movement started here.
A big centre of car manufacturing.
Q170366: Capital of Khuzestan in southwest Iran, on the Karun River, Iran's largest river.
Centre of Iran's oil industry; has a large Arab population.
Known for its many bridges over the Karun.
One of the hottest cities in the world, often above 50 °C in summer.
Q332753: The westernmost city of Shandong, formerly Caozhou.
Called the 'Peony Capital of China', with huge peony fields and a festival every April.
Associated with Song Jiang and the outlaws of 'Water Margin' in nearby Yuncheng.
Q213026: City in Uttar Pradesh on the Ramganga River, in the Rohilkhand region.
Founded in 1537; was capital of the Rohilla Afghans in the 18th century.
Known for the Ala Hazrat dargah, a centre of the Barelvi Sunni movement.
Famous for zari embroidery, furniture and kites ('manjha' kite string).
Q52535: Argentina's third city, on the Paraná River northwest of Buenos Aires.
The Argentine flag was first raised here in 1812; the National Flag Memorial marks the spot.
Birthplace of Che Guevara and Lionel Messi.
A major grain-export port for the Pampas.
Q198061: City in eastern Henan on the Shaying River.
Said to be the ancient capital of the legendary Fuxi; Laozi is believed to have been born in Luyi county nearby.
Once the capital of the Chen and Chu states.
Q26590: The largest city of Chihuahua, on the Rio Grande across from El Paso, Texas.
Called El Paso del Norte until 1888; renamed after President Benito Juárez.
A major maquiladora factory city and one of the busiest border crossings.
Claims to be the birthplace of the burrito.
